nodes.label: Decision 1: process-resources phase for composer invocation
nodes.rationale: process-resources comes immediately after generate-resources (where xml-maven-plugin:transform assembles archetype-metadata.xml) and before package/integration-test — the same site the internal precedent occupies, guaranteeing symmetry; mixing two transformers in generate-resources would be confusing.

nodes.label: Decision 2: pinning Groovy 4.0.28 via plugin <dependencies>
nodes.rationale: Plugin <dependencies> is the standard Maven3 mechanism and adds to the classpath rather than replacing it, so an exclusion is only needed if a conflict appears; empirically gmaven 2.1.1 ran with its default Groovy 2.4.9 and the composer still worked.

nodes.label: Decision 3: two separate import-stripping patterns
nodes.rationale: Separating the pure-import pattern from the commented-import pattern and processing them sequentially is more readable than replicating the POSIX compound regex; the Groovy whitespace class is semantically equivalent to the POSIX space class for ASCII.

nodes.label: Decision 4: alphabetical file order via listFiles().sort
nodes.rationale: File.listFiles().sort { it.name } is equivalent to ls -1 | sort (lexicographic ASCII); an explicit name list would make the composer fragile to any new file added out of order, and semantic-priority ordering adds subjective decisions without clear gain.

nodes.label: Decision 5: generate into target/classes/META-INF/
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the existing strategy for the generated archetype-metadata.xml (excluded from src/main/resources, packaged from target/classes); generating into src/main would mix artifact with source and couple the build to .gitignore configuration.

nodes.label: Decision 6: script_core.sh line 42 is the sole caller (empirical)
nodes.rationale: grep confirmed the only caller of create_archetype_post_generate.sh is script_core.sh (source at line 41, call at line 42) — removing two lines fully detaches the bash pre-processor, so no conditional SKIP flag was needed.

nodes.label: Decision 7: remove the committed archetype-post-generate.groovy monolith
nodes.rationale: Keeping the monolith versioned would make it a divergent source of truth from the build — exactly the anti-pattern the spec avoids; remove it only after byte-equivalence is validated by diff, and investigate any divergence before removing.
